log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 37% BRING: annihilape, 24% BRING: tinkaton, 14% BRING: chandelure
Pick 2: 35% BRING: tinkaton, 27% BRING: chandelure, 24% BRING: palafin
Pick 3: 48% BRING: chandelure, 27% BRING: palafin, 15% BRING: incineroar

Incineroar leads well: Intimidate weakens their physical attackers, and Fake Out and Parting Shot give control. Garchomp adds fast Mega pressure, and Gholdengo covers the Steel and Fire matchups with special power. Together they hit Palafin, Chandelure, and Toxapex well.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick 3 to bring against their Incineroar, Annihilape, Chandelure, Palafin, Toxapex, and Tinkaton. Weighing Incineroar, Garchomp, and Kingambit as strong options, though Kingambit's weakness to Fighting from Annihilape gives me pause while I check matchups against their fire and fairy types.

Gholdengo stands out as a strong special attacker that handles Palafin and Toxapex well, with ground coverage from Garchomp also hitting Toxapex. I'll settle on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Gholdengo as my final three.

decisions.thought: 76% MOVE: closecombat, 22% MOVE: earthquake, 2% SWITCH: tinkaton

Fake Out is useless because Annihilape is Ghost-type and immune to Normal moves. Annihilape is faster, so Flare Blitz is the strongest real damage I can deal before it moves. Its Atk is already at -1 and it shows no Defiant boost, so I'll keep pressure on.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
That "no effect on Annihilape" note clicks for me now — Annihilape is Fighting/Ghost type, and Fake Out is a Normal-type move, so Ghost's immunity to Normal blocks it entirely, not just the flinch.

Flare Blitz hits neutrally and could deal solid damage, but I'm wary since Annihilape may carry Defiant, meaning Incineroar's own Intimidate (and any further stat drops like Parting Shot) could actually buff Annihilape's Attack sharply. Given the uncertainty around Annihilape's ability and that Flare Blitz likely isn't a KO, switching out to something like Gholdengo seems like the safer, more productive play.

So Annihilape's Fighting-type attacks hit Gholdengo for zero damage since Ghost is immune to Fighting, while Gholdengo's Shadow Ball would hit Annihilape super effectively. Given that, Flare Blitz seems like the right call for damage output over Parting Shot.

decisions.thought: 43% MOVE: fireblast [MEGA], 13% MOVE: shadowball [MEGA], 13% MOVE: calmmind [MEGA]

Incineroar has 41 HP and Chandelure is probably faster, so it will likely be KO'd before it can act. Garchomp takes Chandelure's Ghost and Fire hits without a weakness, and it outspeeds Chandelure. Earthquake is super effective on Chandelure's Fire typing, so Garchomp can threaten a KO next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at low HP and Chandelure likely outspeeds, threatening a KO with Shadow Ball or Fire Blast since Flare Blitz won't be effective here. Switching to Gholdengo looks like the safer play given its Steel/Ghost typing.

Shadow Ball could hit Gholdengo for roughly 60-80% given the STAB and type effectiveness stacking against its special defense. Meanwhile Incineroar at 41 HP is nearly dead to anything Chandelure throws out since it's slower—Protect only delays the inevitable, but Parting Shot could at least debuff Chandelure while pivoting safely to Gholdengo.

Switching directly to Gholdengo now seems best since Incineroar is essentially fodder at this point and Gholdengo resists Fire-type pressure well, though Shadow Ball remains its main threat.

Garchomp's Earthquake should nearly OHKO Chandelure given its low HP and Garchomp's high Attack, while Gholdengo would take a hefty Shadow Ball hit instead. Garchomp is clearly the better switch-in, so that's my move.

decisions.thought: 44% MOVE: energyball, 22% SWITCH: tinkaton, 20% MOVE: calmmind

Garchomp outspeeds Mega Chandelure, and Earthquake is 2x super effective against its Fire typing with 100% accuracy. Mega Garchomp's much higher Attack should threaten a knockout before Chandelure moves, and megaing now also adds Sand Force.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Mega Garchomp outspeeds and its Earthquake hits Chandelure for super effective damage since Fire is weak to Ground and Ghost typing offers no immunity there.

Checking the return matchup too—Chandelure's Fire Blast only does half damage to Garchomp since Dragon resists Fire, so mega Garchomp isn't at much risk there.

decisions.thought: 61% MOVE: gigatonhammer, 24% MOVE: swordsdance, 8% MOVE: stealthrock

Tinkaton is Fairy/Steel, so Earthquake is super effective and Mega Garchomp's 222 Attack should do heavy damage. Garchomp is likely faster or close to it, so Earthquake is the strongest reliable hit this turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Tinkaton is Fairy/Steel, so Earthquake hits for 2x since Ground is super effective against Steel. Speed-wise, Mega Garchomp could be faster depending on Tinkaton's spread, and Earthquake with Garchomp's high attack should do heavy damage against Tinkaton's defense range, likely close to a KO. Stone Edge isn't effective here, so Earthquake is clearly the better option.
